hpi_details: 48F reports a firm, painless nodule on her right palm that has been present for 1 year. Over the past 3 months, a tight band has developed, pulling her right ring finger slightly inward toward the palm.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Dupuytren Contracture.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Trigger finger (stenosing tenosynovitis) without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.

history.answer: I noticed a firm bump on my right palm about a year ago, and over the past three months my ring finger has started curling inward toward my palm.
The hard bump in my palm showed up about a year ago, but the finger bending only started about three months ago.
It is right in the center of my right palm, right at the base of my ring finger.
It started out small like a little pea, but over the last three months it developed into a tight band that is pulling my finger down.
There is just this one bump and band on my right palm, and nothing on my other fingers or my left hand.
It feels very hard and tough, like a thick callous or a pebble beneath the skin, and it does not budge when I push on it.
No, it does not hurt at all, even when I press on it firmly.
The skin over it looks a little puckered, but there are no abnormal color changes, dark moles, or new spots.
No, it has never bled, cracked, ulcerated, or formed a scab.
No redness, warmth, swelling, or any kind of foul drainage.
No, there is no central hole, blackhead, or cheesy white material coming out of it.
It stays the exact same size throughout the day; using my hand does not make it swell up, and resting does not make it shrink.
No, I have never had any cuts, punctures, burns, or surgeries on that palm.
No fever, chills, night sweats, or unintentional weight loss.
I work indoors arranging flowers and have not had excessive sun exposure or bad sunburns.
Neither I nor anyone in my family has ever been diagnosed with skin cancer or melanoma.
I am not taking any steroids or immune medications, but I have had type 2 diabetes for about five years.
I have never tried to squeeze, pop, or cut it, and I have not received any medical treatments or injections for it yet.
My ring finger stays bent toward my palm, but it does not catch, click, or snap into place like a trigger finger when I move it.
Yes, over the past three months I can feel a tight cord or string running from the lump toward the base of my ring finger.
When I try to press my right palm completely flat on a table, the palm and ring finger stay lifted and cannot touch the surface.
It is making my florist work difficult because my finger gets caught when I slide on gardening gloves, wash my face, or hold shears.
My father had a similar problem where his little finger slowly curled into his palm as he grew older.
I was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes five years ago, but I have no other chronic medical conditions.
I have never had any surgeries or hospital admissions.
I take metformin 500 milligrams twice a day for my diabetes.
I do not have any allergies to medications, latex, or foods.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used any tobacco products.
I only drink an occasional glass of wine on special occasions, maybe once or twice a month at most.
I work full-time as a florist, and I live in an apartment with my husband and teenage son.
My periods are regular every twenty-eight days, my last period was two weeks ago, I have an IUD, and there is no possibility of pregnancy.
I wondered if it might be a tendon strain from cutting stems all day or perhaps a benign cyst.
I am really worried that my finger will curl further inward and I will permanently lose the use of my right hand.
I was hoping to get an evaluation and a referral to a hand specialist to see what options exist to straighten my finger.

exam.finding: Blood pressure is 122/78 mmHg, pulse 72 beats per minute, respiratory rate 14 breaths per minute, oxygen saturation 99% on room air, and temperature 36.6 °C.
The patient is alert, comfortable, and in no acute distress, holding her right hand naturally in her lap.

A firm, non-tender 1-centimeter nodule with skin puckering and a visible longitudinal fibrous cord is present on the right palm aligned with the fourth ray; no erythema, warmth, or skin lesions elsewhere.

Fixed 20-degree flexion contracture at the right fourth metacarpophalangeal joint with a positive tabletop test where the palm cannot lay flat, while the interphalangeal joints and left hand demonstrate full passive motion.
Grip strength and intrinsic hand muscle power are 5/5 bilaterally, with active extension of the right ring finger limited solely by the mechanical cord.
Intact light touch and two-point discrimination along all digital nerve distributions of both hands.
Radial and ulnar pulses are 2+ bilaterally with capillary refill under two seconds in all fingertips.
Axillary examination reveals no palpable lymphadenopathy or tenderness bilaterally.
